events.line: A gale kept every boat on the quay and the day's catch with it.
A squall came up out of nowhere. You lost the day's catch, never the boat.
A shoal of mackerel came through so thick the skipper reckoned you could walk across it.
A seal helped itself to the best of the catch and looked entirely unrepentant.
Day trippers paid for a trip round the bay and left a tip, mostly in fudge.
The engine coughed twice and quit. Half a day's fishing with the oars and a lot of language.
Visitors begged a dolphin-spotting trip round the harbour mouth. The dolphin was shy, the visitors were not.

upgrades.name: Bigger nets and a second hand
upgrades.text: A bigger haul, and a wage to pay whether the fish come or not.

upgrades.name: An ice hold and a cold store
upgrades.text: The catch arrives fresher, and a rough week costs you less.

upgrades.name: A permanent berth on the pier
upgrades.text: No more circling for a space, and the wall between you and the weather. Harbour dues, though.

asks.title: The ice machine on the pier
asks.text: The ice machine on the pier has broken down again, and the fish will not wait for it. {deed} is in for a warm week.

options.label: Hire a van of ice from the next harbour
options.say: Costly, cold and it works. The fish go to market looking like they have been on holiday.

options.label: Sell the catch the same day at the quay
options.say: Sold by the afternoon at a lower price. Nobody on the quay is sorry.

options.label: Wait for the council to mend it
options.say: The council mends it on Thursday of the following week.
